_comment: What is up for auction. Read once at startup by listings.py; see the
Each listing: title, url, and optionally blurb, note, sold, photos.
The first photo is the hero, shown large; the rest go in a grid under it.
Every photo needs alt text - the page is almost entirely images.
Photos live in static/auction/ and must be in the repository, since that
is how install.sh gets them onto the container. STRIP THE EXIF: phone
pictures taken at home carry GPS.

listings.title: The first frame
listings.blurb: Around a hundred receipts sent to this printer by strangers, mounted behind glass. No theme and no editing - whatever turned up.

photos.alt: A large dark wood picture frame filled with about a hundred thermal receipts, each headed INCOMING with a timestamp, arranged in columns.
Detail of the top-left of the frame: individual receipts showing a message about brighter days, an ASCII map of Australia, a drawing of a girl with a mug, and a Bobby Tables SQL-injection joke.
photos.caption: Top left. The one about brighter days came from someone who signed off only as "someone on the internet".

photos.alt: Detail of the lower right of the frame, showing dithered pixel-art receipts including a rabbit, a footballer and several ASCII drawings.
photos.caption: Lower right. Braille art gets decoded back into a bitmap and printed as a picture, which is why these are dots and not characters.

photos.alt: The frame held up at an angle in a living room, with a second smaller framed collage visible on the wall behind it.
photos.caption: For scale. The smaller frame behind it is not included.
